newsitem.title: MEXICO: FORECAST - Analyst see weak ICA Q1 report.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Analyst see weak ICA Q1 report.

text.p: Mexican builder Empresas ICA has seen its share prices fall 8.5 percent since April 7, as the market anticipated a weak first quarter report, analysts said.
An average of six industry analysts consulted by Reuters estimated an average earning per share of 0.032 peso compared with 2.42 pesos for the same period in 1996.
However, analysts said the key to determining ICA's earnings per share was anticipating the monetary position and the company's highway concession losses.
"In general, ICA is seen reporting weak revenues and profits, but that is no surprise," Goldman Sachs analyst in New York Chris Hussey said.
Said Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Mexico City analyst Gordon Lee: "They are weak, especially on the operating level, but I don't think the results set a trend."
Industry observers noted that ICA's profitability margins were hurt, hit by initial burdens of new projects.
"Initial work charges affected costs and operating expenses and the fact is because ICA is so big it takes longer to see revenue," ING Barings New York analyst Hector Castillo said.

Ben Uglow, from Robert Fleming Research in New York, estimated an operating margin for ICA of 3.5 percent, on income of 1.584 billion pesos, down 28.2 percent from the previous quarter. Net profit will be about four million pesos, he estimated.
In addition to anticipating first quarter results, the markets are also waiting for news of the level of ICA's backlog, which could affect the stock price, analysts said.
"The company could report a backlog of 5.739 billion pesos, down 5.6 percent compared with the end of 1996," Serfin brokerage analyst Gerardo Saenz said in a report.
